How SentinelOps Works

The complete 4-step workflow that decouples deep telemetry gathering from cloud data sharing.

1

Local Telemetry Scraping (Tier 1)

The SentinelOps local collector runs as a lightweight Docker container or Python service inside your VPC. Every 5 seconds, it gathers CPU, memory, disk, network, and application health telemetry using psutil. Raw metrics are committed locally to an encrypted SQLite database.

2

Privacy Engine & Fail-Closed Sanitization

Telemetry streams are passed to the Privacy Engine. Multi-pattern regex scrubbers strip emails, tokens, API keys, and IPs. An allowlist validator constructs new objects; any unvetted field or raw log line is rejected and logged to a local audit trail.

3

Cryptographic Signing & Secure Outbound HTTPS

The approved statistical summaries (p50/p95/p99) and health metrics are signed with HMAC-SHA256 using the organization's secret key. The collector transmits the payload to the SaaS endpoint over outbound HTTPS. No inbound firewall ports are ever opened.

4

Cloud AIOps Intelligence & Fleet Dashboards (Tier 2)

The FastAPI backend validates the HMAC signature and schema (rejecting any unknown fields). The AIOps engine runs correlation RCA, detects cross-service incident cascades, and visualizes health in the Next.js dark-navy dashboard.
